For example, you can\\nallow Connect Customer to access an Amazon Lex V2 bot.\\n\\nTo learn how to create a bot or bot alias, see Working with Amazon Lex V2 bots.\\n\\n###### Topics\\n\\n* Use the console to specify a resource-based policy\\n* Use the API to specify a resource-based policy\\n* Allow an IAM role to update a bot and list bot aliases\\n* Allow a user to have a conversation with a bot\\n* Allow an AWS service to use a specific Amazon Lex V2 bot\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lexv2/latest/dg/security_iam_resource-based-policy-examples.html\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"Streamline Amazon Lex V2 bot development and deployment by using an automated workflow\",\"context\":\"## Troubleshooting\\n\\n| Issue | Solution |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| When you deploy Amazon Lex bots to different AWS accounts, the tooling services must have the necessary permissions to access resources in those accounts. | To grant cross-account access, use IAM roles and policies. For more information, see IAM permissions required to import and IAM permissions required to export bots in Lex V2 in the Amazon Lex documentation. |\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/patterns/streamline-amazon-lex-bot-development-and-deployment-using-an-automated-workflow.html\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Look up AWS docs on Lex V2 bot resource-based policies for cross-account access."}

{"id": "7d41f3f7-cb99-4ad6-ac8f-d8b90e363a8e", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "The key fact here: **you can't do this with a resource-based policy at all.** AWS documentation is explicit:

> "You can't use cross-account or cross-region policies with Amazon Lex V2. If you create a policy for a resource with a cross-account or cross-region ARN, Amazon Lex V2 returns an error."

So a bot/bot-alias resource-based policy naming a principal from account `012345678901_4` on a bot in `012345678901_1` will be rejected outright — Lex V2 resource policies only support same-account principals.

**What to use instead** for cross-account `lex:RecognizeText` access, per AWS's recommended pattern:

1. **In the bot's account (012345678901_1):** Create an IAM role that trusts account `012345678901_4` (or a specific role/user in it), with a permissions policy granting `lex:RecognizeText` (and `lex:RecognizeUtterance` if needed) scoped to the bot/bot-alias ARN.
2. **In the caller's account (012345678901_4):** Grant the caller permission to `sts:AssumeRole` on that role.
3. The caller assumes the role in 012345678901_1, then calls `RecognizeText` using those temporary credentials — standard cross-account role assumption, not a resource-based bot policy.

If you want, I can draft the actual trust policy and permissions policy JSON for that role — just confirm the bot's ARN (or bot ID/alias ID) and whether the caller side is an IAM role or IAM user in 012345678901_4.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
